methods.label: Use the sum of the bisected angles
methods.explanation:
We need only the sum of the angles at \(A\) and \(C\), because both are halved in triangle \(ADC\). The angle sum in triangle \(ABC\) gives
\[
\angle BAC+\angle BCA=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ.
\]
Since \(AD\) and \(CD\) bisect these angles,
\[
\angle DAC+\angle ACD
=\frac12(\angle BAC+\angle BCA)
=65^\circ.
\]
The three angles of triangle \(ADC\) also sum to \(180^\circ\). Therefore
\[
\angle ADC=180^\circ-65^\circ=\boxed{115^\circ},
\]
which is choice C.
